section: General Knowledge & CA · Ch3 — Indian Polity
subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: Which Fundamental Right is available only to Indian citizens and not to foreigners?

options.option_text: Right against discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex (Article 15)
Right to Life and Personal Liberty (Article 21)

explanation: Article 15 (non-discrimination) is available only to citizens. Articles 14, 21 and 23 use the word 'person', extending protection to citizens and foreigners alike.

section: General Knowledge & CA · Ch3 — Indian Polity
subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: During a National Emergency under Article 352, which Fundamental Right cannot be suspended under any circumstances?

options.option_text: Right to life and personal liberty (Article 21), and Article 20
Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) always remains fully unrestricted
All rights are suspended without exception

explanation: Following the 44th Amendment, Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during an Emergency. Article 19 is automatically suspended only during a National Emergency on grounds of war/external aggression.

section: General Knowledge & CA · Ch3 — Indian Polity
subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: The lower house of a State Legislature (where it exists as bicameral) is called the:
explanation: The Legislative Assembly is the state's lower (directly elected) house; the Legislative Council, where it exists, is the upper house. Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha are the Union Parliament's houses.

section: General Knowledge & CA · Ch3 — Indian Polity
subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: Under the 73rd Amendment, the three-tier Panchayati Raj structure consists of the Gram Panchayat, the intermediate level, and the:
explanation: The three tiers are Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti/Mandal Parishad (block/intermediate), and Zilla Parishad (district). Municipal bodies belong to the separate 74th Amendment urban framework.

section: General Knowledge & CA · Ch3 — Indian Polity
subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: The Chief Election Commissioner of India can be removed from office only through a process similar to the removal of a:

options.option_text: State Governor, by the President at will
Ordinary government employee, by disciplinary action

explanation: Article 324 gives the CEC security of tenure equivalent to a Supreme Court judge — removable only via a Parliamentary process (impeachment-like), safeguarding the Election Commission's independence.

section: General Knowledge & CA · Ch3 — Indian Polity
subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: The CAG's reports on the accounts of the Union are submitted to:

options.option_text: The President, who causes them to be laid before Parliament
The Prime Minister directly, with no further action
The Supreme Court for judicial review first

explanation: CAG reports on Union accounts go to the President, who lays them before Parliament (examined further by the Public Accounts Committee); state-level reports go via the Governor to the State Legislature.
